UC-MOD-001.how: New lib/reading.js states a reading protocol (status, view, frame, words, input, carrySession, signIn, signInSafari, signInStatus, retry, close) built by createReadingSurface({reader}); lib/daemon.js composes it as this.reading; lib/server.js now goes through daemon.reading and names zero members of the Reader, down from 33 including the three plain fields the finding calls out (seq, running, signingIn). The reader's own sequencing moved with it, which is the part that mattered: the ensure/recover-a-lost-session/capture/read-ahead order, the input dispatch and the repaint wait all now live in the reading module rather than inside route bodies, so a reading-surface bug is read in lib/reading.js plus lib/reader.js instead of in four files. Deliberately NOT done: wrapping daemon.panel.* and daemon.engine.* the same way. Those are already narrow method surfaces on small classes (Panel is 366 lines, and the reach-throughs are show/state/ping and advance/standDown/resumeDay); a 1:1 wrapper around them would be ceremony rather than decoupling, and the finding's stated cost, having to read the 1747-line Reader to understand a route, does not apply to them.

UC-CUPID-002.how: Refuted as out of scope for this loop, not as untrue. The finding is accurate: lib/reader.js is 1747 lines and class Reader does browser lifecycle, Amazon sign-in, session carry, viewport fitting, capture with a prefetch shelf, OCR, input injection and shelf listing. The reason not to split it here is specific to this repo. The halves that would move across the split are exactly the halves nothing can exercise without a live headless Chrome and a live signed-in Amazon session: test/reader.test.js and test/reader-shelf.test.js are substantial (46 tests) but cover the pure helpers, the shelf arithmetic and stubbed-CDP paths, and nothing in test/ ever reaches #start (line 744), carry (651), reauthenticate (697), clearSiteData or #applyViewport (931). On this machine the reader cannot even be driven right now: POST /api/reading/view against the live daemon answers 'the reader browser never opened its debugging port: fetch failed', so a split could not have been behaviourally verified in this loop at all, only claimed. Splitting a class whose riskiest third has no reachable coverage, at the end of a 63-row audit loop, would trade a stated design defect for an unstated behavioural one, and CLAUDE.md's own rule for this repo is that the reader's failure paths must stay specific and remedy-bearing. What was done instead is the part that removes the cost the finding names: lib/reading.js pins a protocol between the HTTP layer and the Reader, so when the split does happen only one file moves with it (see UC-MOD-001).
UC-CUPID-002.verified: Evidence for the coverage claim: `grep -c '^test(' test/reader.test.js test/reader-shelf.test.js` gives 25 and 21; none of them constructs a Reader that launches a browser (every `new Reader({config:{reading:{}}})` in those files exercises pure methods or stubbed CDP). Evidence for the not-drivable claim: live `POST /api/reading/view` returns error 'the reader browser never opened its debugging port: fetch failed'. Full suite 336/336, exit 0, with lib/reader.js unchanged in this loop (`git status --short lib/reader.js` is empty).

UC-CUPID-003.how: Both hidden caches are now visible at the call site. lib/config.js `load` is renamed `loadCached`, because the memo was the whole surprise of it: the name read as 'go and read the file' while the second call after an edit returned the first call's answer, and `defaults()` was already there for a caller who wants the file as it is on disk. Six call sites updated (lib/doctor.js, lib/install.js, four in bin/interstice.js) plus test/video-whitelist-reload.test.js. lib/state/companions.js `cache` stopped being a module-level mutable and became an ordinary defaulted parameter: `companionsSnapshot(config, {force, overrides, cache = moduleCache})` and `invalidateCompanions(cache = moduleCache)`, so the ambient state a caller reads is in the signature and a test can pass its own cache instead of inheriting whatever an earlier test left behind. Real callers pass nothing and share the module cache, so behaviour is unchanged.
UC-CUPID-003.verified: `grep -rn '\bload(' lib bin test | grep -v loadCached` returns nothing outside unrelated identifiers. Full suite 336/336 including test/companions.test.js and test/companions-control.test.js, exit 0. Live daemon restarted on the renamed function and answers health 200.

UC-CMT-001.how: Both sleeps are gone rather than merely commented, which is the second of the two fixes the finding offers. The reader already knows when the page has repainted: #hold bumps `seq` only when the JPEG bytes differ. lib/reading.js afterInput() re-photographs at 60ms and returns the instant seq moves, with REPAINT_BUDGET_MS = 600 as a documented ceiling rather than a measurement, and the response now carries `repainted` and `waitedMs` so 'that click did nothing' is a fact the panel can see instead of being indistinguishable from success. The comment says exactly that: both 350 and 250 were the same guess at Amazon's repaint time, and a guess is wrong in both directions. I did not claim a measurement for either number because I have none.
UC-CMT-001.verified: `grep -n 'setTimeout(t, [0-9]' lib/server.js` prints nothing. test/reading-input-repaint.test.js: 'an input returns as soon as the page repaints, not after a fixed sleep' returns in 79ms (inside the 600ms ceiling) with repainted:true and the post-repaint seq; 'an input that changes nothing gives up at the ceiling and says it changed nothing' waits >=600ms and answers repainted:false. That second test caught a real bug I introduced while moving the code (seq was read before the repaint was awaited, so the answer carried the sequence of the picture taken before the input landed); fixed in lib/reading.js and the test now passes.

UC-PRIN-002.how: Re-checked against current code as instructed, and it was two thirds resolved and one third worse than the finding described. Resolved before this loop: lib/focus/tracker.js composes createMachine and all three breakers, and lib/daemon.js starts the tracker and builds createLatency/latencyEventFromEngine, so those six have real non-test callers. Closed by this loop: initialState was still exported with no caller anywhere, and is now module-internal (see UC-PRIN-003). Found and fixed by this loop: the video wiring existed but did not work. The tracker passed `probe: probeVideo` while the breaker calls `probe()` with no arguments, and probeVideo destructures its options, so every tick threw 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading browsers)', the tracker's catch turned it into a warning and a no-break, and the video breaker had been silently off for as long as it had been wired in: four warnings a minute in logs/launchd.err.log and never one forfeit. A caller that exists but cannot be called is the same as no caller, which is this finding. The tracker now calls probeVideo({browsers: focus.videoBrowsers, connect}) with `connect` from lib/cdp.js, and config/interstice.config.default.json ships a new `focus.videoBrowsers: []` documented in README.md: there is no way to discover the debugging endpoint of a browser that was not started with one, so an empty list means no endpoints, no records and no break, which is the honest state rather than an exception pretending to be one.

The headline assertion is the one the rule names: a scan of nothing but synthetic gaps aggregates to exactly zero (totals.gaps 0, minutesReclaimed 0, delivered 0, deliveryRate 0 rather than NaN, byRung {}, bySurface {}) while totals.synthetic counts them and the rows are still in the table. Around it: every headline figure is asserted against a number computed by hand in the comment beside it (deliveryRate, minutesReclaimed from first delivery to end, median and p90 index arithmetic, belowArm against config.arm, two-rung counting, false positives from both causes, stand-down rate, per-surface counts), the false-positive window is pinned in both directions, and suggestThresholds is pinned on both sides of its minSample gate. No shape was invented: REAL_KEYS and REAL_DELIVERY_KEYS are asserted against the daemon's own logs/gaps.jsonl (2070 records on this machine), in both directions, so a fixture that carries a field no real record has fails; every fixture is written with appendJsonl and read back with readJsonl, the same path the routes use; and one test runs summarize over the real log and asserts totals.gaps + totals.synthetic equals the record count. PS-007.how: docs/audit/route.py no longer names a single file of this repo. It takes --target (or TARGET_REPO) and errors without one; it asks the repo what it contains via `git ls-files`, falling back to a walk that honours .gitignore plus a skip set; and it clusters the result by directory, keeping each directory whole, so the UX and JS batch localities are computed rather than typed. The web/learn.html that never existed is gone with the rest of the hardcoding. Using git rather than a bare walk is load-bearing here: this repo keeps two live Chrome profiles under logs/, and the first version of the walk routed 5,002 vendored extension files as the product, which is a worse wrong answer than the hardcoded list it replaced. Batch fan-out is now driven by two target-agnostic numbers, how many localities there are and MAX_ROWS_PER_BATCH, instead of the literals 48 and 58. docs/recurring_goals_selection.py's RECURRING_GOALS_ROOT and TARGET_REPO are required rather than defaulted to one machine's absolute paths, and refuse with a named remedy when unset or not a directory.
PS-007.verified: With no target: `python3 docs/audit/route.py` prints 'route.py: error: no target repo: pass --target /path/to/repo or set TARGET_REPO'.
